# Security invariants

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_invariants_doc.py from security/invariants.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Each invariant is a testable statement tied to the threat model (`THREAT_MODEL.md`). `security/invariants.json` is the source of truth; `scripts/check_invariants.py` fails CI if a mapped test disappears, and the full test suite fails CI if any mapped test fails.

**Status meanings.** `automated`: exercised by tests at the stated scope. `partial`: tested at the stated scope, with the gap listed. `manual`: cannot be automated here.

| ID | Invariant | Status | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| SEC-004 | Object storage only receives client-side encrypted attachments. | partial | 3 |

| SEC-020 | The Kotlin/FFI boundary exposes no key material or raw MLS state, treats every Kotlin input as hostile, and a Rust panic never crosses into Kotlin. | partial | 7 |
| SEC-021 | Every Android window is FLAG_SECURE (dialogs included), only one component is exported, there are no deep links, WebViews, backups or cleartext traffic, and release builds are non-debuggable and refuse a software Keystore. | partial | 9 |
| SEC-022 | Group authorisation is enforced by every receiver before a commit is merged; the relay is not trusted for authorisation, and a forged commit does not brick the group. | automated | 5 |
| SEC-023 | Concurrent group commits are ordered deterministically and atomically by the relay's compare-and-swap sequencer; losers rebase; out-of-order or withheld commits are held, not misapplied; removal rotates the routing tag. | automated | 8 |
| SEC-024 | Notification text never reveals content while the vault is locked, whatever the privacy mode; the default mode shows neither sender nor content; the wake payload is the exact constant. | partial | 5 |
| SEC-025 | Cipher IDs are random, not derived from any key/phone/email, and have exactly one canonical spelling; contacts are added only by Cipher ID or QR, and a replaced identity key is never accepted silently. | automated | 6 |
| SEC-026 | The experimental key-transparency verifier cannot mark a contact verified or override manual verification, and rejects forged/rolled-back/forked/malformed log evidence. NOT PRODUCTION READY: feature-gated, no log, not wired in. | partial | 7 |
| SEC-027 | The relay on PostgreSQL stays bounded and consistent: forward-only checksummed migrations, shared rate limits and replay protection across instances, exact bounded queues, atomic operations, load shedding. | automated | 9 |
| SEC-028 | Restoring an older copy of the app's local storage is detected and refused (monotonic generation held outside the data directory); the vault is not used afterwards. | partial | 7 |
| SEC-029 | Attacker-controlled media (thumbnails, images, audio, video, PDF) can never crash the app or exhaust its memory: headers are checked, decoding is sub-sampled, failures degrade to 'cannot display'. | partial | 5 |
| SEC-030 | A fully compromised relay and database cannot read content or silently change authenticated conversation state: tampering, redirection, duplication, replay, epoch rollback, fake acknowledgements, partitions, tag retirement and counter resets are prevented or detected, with the undetectable cases documented. | partial | 10 |
| SEC-031 | The relay bounds attacker-controlled resource use BEFORE expensive work: large uploads are authenticated before their body is read, concurrent uploads are capped, and KeyPackage claims are limited per target and per requester. | partial | 6 |
| SEC-032 | A device record is bound to its account: the identity key signs account, device and auth key together, so a record cannot be replayed under another account id. | automated | 3 |
| SEC-033 | Forward secrecy is durable: ratchet advances caused by receiving messages are persisted before the relay is told to forget the ciphertext and before locking, so the state on disk cannot re-derive consumed message keys. | partial | 1 |
| SEC-034 | The app's transport refuses downgrade (TLS 1.2), expired, wrong-host and untrusted-CA certificates (what a MITM proxy presents), never follows a redirect to HTTP and never speaks plain HTTP. | partial | 8 |
| SEC-035 | A lock request (background, screen off, manual) never waits behind a running operation: in-flight network calls and transfers are aborted first, then the vault locks. | partial | 3 |
| SEC-036 | The Keystore wrapper never RETURNS the vault key to Kotlin code and zeroes its own copies; a keystore that delivers nothing cannot unlock the vault. (Mitigates ST-027; does not eliminate it.) | partial | 3 |
| SEC-037 | Input and overlay surfaces are hardened: typed text avoids keyboard learning/autofill, touches are dropped under overlays, system overlays are hidden, non-tool accessibility services are denied (API 34+), and saved state never holds secrets. | partial | 4 |
| SEC-038 | Names and preview lines cannot disguise themselves: control characters, bidirectional overrides/embeddings/isolates, zero-width spaces and similar format characters are refused in group names by every receiver and stripped from contact names, previews and notifications; emoji joiners and RTL text remain valid. | partial | 2 |
| REV-001 | A removed member cannot decrypt group messages sent after the removal commit, nor send messages other members accept. | partial | 3 |
| REV-002 | After a removed member's compliant Cipher client observes the removal, it cannot decrypt Cipher-retained pre-removal history: the decryption operation itself fails (all per-epoch history keys are deleted, vault holds no plaintext). | partial | 7 |
| REV-003 | Remaining members retain the history they were authorised to read across removals, restarts and concurrent traffic. | automated | 5 |
| REV-004 | A removed member cannot restore membership or history access from stale local state: a restored old vault is refused at unlock, a replayed Welcome is rejected by the revocation tombstone, and only a newer legitimate Welcome gives access to the NEW era. | partial | 2 |
| REV-005 | The relay cannot independently restore a removed member's access or make the compliant client retain it: replayed Welcomes/commits and misrouted ciphertext are useless; withholding the removal only delays revocation and never yields new content. | partial | 3 |
| REV-006 | Removal advances the MLS epoch and therefore the history-access key; a committer whose response was lost converges on the same epoch instead of diverging. | partial | 2 |
| REV-007 | Removal rotates the relay routing capability: the old tag is retired and cannot be used to advance the group. | automated | 2 |
| REV-008 | Removal is account-level: the commit removes every device (MLS leaf) of the removed account. | partial | 1 |
| REV-009 | A device that has been removed from a group receives no future group secrets. | partial | 2 |
| REV-010 | A relay acknowledgement cannot masquerade as a recipient's cryptographic receipt: Delivered is set only by an end-to-end receipt from the recipient. | partial | 1 |
| PRIV-001 | Message plaintext remains protected independently of the privacy transport: the transport (and every node behind it) only ever carries E2EE ciphertext inside TLS. | partial | 3 |
| PRIV-002 | The final Cipher delivery relay does not normally receive the client's source IP: the connection it sees comes from the privacy route's egress. | partial | 2 |
| PRIV-003 | In a multi-hop mode no single privacy node normally learns both the client's address and the final Cipher destination. | manual | 0 |
| PRIV-004 | Long-lived stable routing identifiers are avoided where possible: contacts deliver with random, rotating, revocable capabilities instead of the recipient's device id and their own authenticated identity. | partial | 3 |
| PRIV-005 | Transport failures never trigger a silent direct-to-Cipher fallback: with the privacy route down the request fails, the encrypted message stays queued, and the destination is never contacted. | partial | 4 |
| PRIV-006 | Privacy mode fails closed: a malformed, refusing or unreachable proxy is a failure, never a working route. | partial | 3 |
| PRIV-007 | DNS resolution does not bypass the privacy path: the relay's name is handed to the proxy, local DNS is disabled, the proxy itself is an IP literal. | partial | 3 |
| PRIV-008 | Application and relay logs contain no route secrets, capabilities, ids, IPs or bodies; the relay writes no per-request line by default and rounds any timestamp to the minute. | partial | 2 |
| PRIV-009 | Message padding remains authenticated and cannot change message semantics: frames are padded with zeros to a size class (1 KiB minimum) inside the MLS ciphertext; the decoder rejects any non-zero or extra padding. | partial | 3 |
| PRIV-010 | The privacy transport (and a delivery capability) cannot decrypt Cipher messages: no key material crosses the transport seam and capabilities grant only the right to queue ciphertext. | automated | 3 |
| PRIV-011 | Network-path selection cannot disable E2EE: there is no setting, profile or route that changes message encryption, and no insecure-transport switch exists in release. | automated | 3 |
| PRIV-012 | Push payload remains content-free: only the exact constant wake-up is accepted; no sender, title, type or filename can be carried. | partial | 2 |
| PRIV-013 | The privacy status shown to the user reflects the actual routing state: Protected only after a request completed through the route recently. | partial | 1 |
| PRIV-014 | A compromised final relay cannot recover the original source IP from application-layer fields: no request body or header Cipher builds contains an address. | partial | 1 |
| PRIV-015 | No direct fallback occurs when all privacy routes are unavailable (engine and release artifact). | partial | 2 |
| PRIV-016 | Delivery capabilities are unguessable, rotate, can be revoked and expire; a stranger flood cannot starve capability holders; replay is idempotent and bounded. | partial | 4 |
| PRIV-017 | Cover traffic is bounded, content-free and cannot trigger actions: at most one dummy delivery per tick, random bytes of the real size class, answered `invalid` and stored nowhere. | partial | 3 |
| MR-001 | A contact card is signed by the issuer's root identity key: flipping any single bit, truncating, extending, retargeting its relay/capability, expiring it or lengthening its lifetime makes it unusable; an onion relay cannot be named without a certificate pin. | automated | 8 |
| MR-002 | A hostile relay cannot substitute a contact's keys on another relay: the directory answer must contain the card's root key with a valid binding signature before anything is pinned or stored. | automated | 2 |
| MR-003 | Intro capabilities open exactly three things at the issuer's relay (device records, KeyPackage claims for the issuer's own devices, delivery); ordinary, unknown, expired and revoked capabilities are one indistinguishable not-found; KeyPackage draining and live card count are bounded. | automated | 6 |
| MR-004 | Alice on relay A and Bob on relay B exchange messages in both directions, in order, including while either is offline, with end-to-end receipts; neither relay holds any record of the other relay's user and no relay-to-relay contact exists. | automated | 3 |
| MR-005 | A message is never reported as sent while nothing left the device: if the peer's relay is unreachable it stays Pending and is delivered after the relay returns; a remote peer is never reached through the authenticated path (whose `not_found` would count as delivered). | automated | 2 |
| MR-006 | Cross-relay attachments (image, PDF, video, voice, arbitrary file, thumbnails) are encrypted before upload, stored by both relays as ciphertext only, downloaded by the recipient from his own relay, and fail closed when tampered, truncated, swapped or missing; uploads need a live capability and respect per-capability and global quotas. | automated | 4 |
| MR-007 | Metadata exposure of first contact is measured: against the mailbox relay, a card-based cross-relay first contact exposes zero signed requests, zero initiator-to-target links, zero stored mentions of the initiator's ids and zero sender hashes. | partial | 1 |
| MR-008 | A conversation that arrives as a message request gets its delivery receipts once accepted, and outgoing timestamps are strictly increasing so same-millisecond messages keep their order. | automated | 2 |
| MR-009 | The Android TLS trust component cannot become an accept-all manager: the platform trust manager decides for every host without a pin, a pin compares the full SPKI SHA-256 in constant time with validity dates, and no other file may touch trust-manager or socket-factory APIs. | partial | 2 |
| MR-010 | Under seeded fault injection (network flaps, responses lost after the relay executed the request, device restarts, relay restarts, clock jumps, same-tick sends) every message reaches the recipient exactly once, in send order, and ends Delivered; messages queued offline leave in encryption order so no generation is lost to MLS out-of-order limits. | automated | 3 |

## SEC-001 — Application servers never receive message plaintext.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A3
* **Scope tested:** Fixture-based: the relay API has no type that can carry plaintext; end-to-end flows are captured on the wire, in the relay DB and in logs.
* **Known gap:** A modified/malicious CLIENT can always send plaintext it chooses to; this guards the shipped client+relay.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_001_005_010_relay_wire_db_and_logs_contain_no_plaintext_or_private_keys` (Rust)
  * `one_to_one_roundtrip_and_ciphertext_hides_plaintext` (Rust)

## SEC-002 — Servers never possess private cryptographic material able to decrypt conversations.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A3
* **Scope tested:** Relay manifest and transitive graph contain no MLS/AEAD/KDF crates (CI script); no client private key appears on the wire, in the relay DB or in logs.
* **Known gap:** None at this scope; key-escrow/backup features added later must be re-evaluated.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_002_relay_crate_has_no_client_crypto_dependencies` (Rust)
  * `sec_001_005_010_relay_wire_db_and_logs_contain_no_plaintext_or_private_keys` (Rust)
  * `scripts/check-relay-deps.sh` (script)

## SEC-003 — A production database dump alone is insufficient to decrypt conversation history.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A3
* **Scope tested:** All queued ciphertext, key packages and directory records are given to an attacker client that cannot decrypt.
* **Known gap:** A dump plus a device compromise is out of scope (see THREAT_MODEL A13).
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_003_full_database_dump_is_insufficient_to_decrypt_history` (Rust)

## SEC-004 — Object storage only receives client-side encrypted attachments.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A4
* **Scope tested:** Blob store content equals client ciphertext; no plaintext/filename/MIME/key in storage; tampering fails closed.
* **Known gap:** The relay can check the container header and size but cannot prove a body is encrypted; a malicious client could upload plaintext.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_004_object_storage_receives_only_ciphertext_and_tampering_fails_closed` (Rust)
  * `storage_provider_sees_only_ciphertext` (Rust)
  * `blob_endpoint_enforces_container_header_and_size_limits` (Rust)

## SEC-005 — Network interception does not reveal message plaintext.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A1, A5
* **Scope tested:** Every byte crossing the client/relay transport is captured and searched; relay TLS config is 1.3-only and refuses TLS 1.2 and untrusted certificates.
* **Known gap:** TLS enforcement in the Android networking stack (OEM variants) and certificate pinning are not tested (no physical-device testing). E2EE does not depend on TLS.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_001_005_010_relay_wire_db_and_logs_contain_no_plaintext_or_private_keys` (Rust)
  * `server_negotiates_tls13_and_refuses_tls12_and_untrusted_certs` (Rust)

## SEC-006 — Removal from a group prevents the removed member from obtaining access to messages from later epochs.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A9
* **Scope tested:** Removed member cannot decrypt or send in later epochs, even with a pre-removal state snapshot and even if the relay misroutes ciphertext to them.
* **Known gap:** Messages the member legitimately decrypted before removal remain known to them. Commit ordering/fork resolution across concurrent committers is not implemented.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_006_removed_member_cannot_read_later_epochs_and_cannot_send` (Rust)
  * `sec_006_removed_member_with_old_state_snapshot_still_cannot_read_new_epoch` (Rust)
  * `sec_006_removed_member_cannot_decrypt_post_removal_even_if_relay_forwards_it` (Rust)

## SEC-007 — Compromise of a current messaging key does not expose all historical messages (forward secrecy).

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A13
* **Scope tested:** Full current client state cannot decrypt already-consumed messages (replay cache cleared to isolate the cryptographic layer). Post-compromise security: after the victim issues a self-update commit, a holder of the old state cannot follow the new epoch or read its traffic.
* **Known gap:** Properties are those of MLS (RFC 9420): keys for not-yet-received out-of-order messages are retained until used; local plaintext history is protected only by the vault, not by ratcheting. PCS only takes effect when members actually issue update commits; automatic scheduling is not implemented yet.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_007_forward_secrecy_current_state_cannot_decrypt_past_messages` (Rust)
  * `sec_007_post_compromise_security_after_self_update_old_state_loses_access` (Rust)

## SEC-008 — Long-term private identity keys are never stored in plaintext in ordinary application storage.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A6, A7, A14
* **Scope tested:** Identity/transport private keys appear only inside vault-encrypted records; the Rust FFI never returns them; Android static guards forbid ordinary storage APIs (SharedPreferences, DataStore, external storage); an emulator run searched the app's whole data directory for fixtures (0 hits).
* **Known gap:** In-memory MLS provider state is not zeroized on drop (OpenMLS memory storage); the 32-byte vault key transits JVM memory during Keystore unwrap (ST-027); hardware backing is not verified on a physical device (ST-001).
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_008_identity_private_material_never_in_plaintext_on_disk` (Rust)
  * `every_activity_extends_secure_activity_and_nothing_clears_the_flag` (Rust)
  * `banned_apis_do_not_appear_in_app_code` (Rust)
  * `vaultFileNeverContainsThePin` (Kotlin, `android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/cipher/messenger/EngineLifecycleInstrumentedTest.kt`)

## SEC-009 — Sensitive local storage is encrypted and its protection is tied to OS/hardware key protection where supported.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A6, A7
* **Scope tested:** Records are AEAD-sealed under a DEK wrapped by the keystore; location binding, corruption and wrong-key cases fail closed; lock lifecycle drops keys.
* **Known gap:** Hardware binding is provided by the Android Keystore, exercised only on an emulator (software-backed). Per-use biometrics, StrongBox and enrolment-change invalidation are NOT TESTED on hardware (ST-001). Rollback of individual records by a file-write attacker is not detected (ST-016).
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_009_database_file_contains_no_plaintext_and_roundtrips_after_unlock` (Rust)
  * `corrupted_record_ciphertext_is_detected_never_returned` (Rust)
  * `records_cannot_be_swapped_between_locations` (Rust)
  * `lifecycle_states_and_keys_unreachable_when_not_unlocked` (Rust)
  * `pin_unlock_requires_the_hardware_bound_secret` (Rust)
  * `wrapUnwrapRoundTripsAndBindsTheAad` (Kotlin, `android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/cipher/messenger/KeystoreInstrumentedTest.kt`)
  * `keyMaterialIsNotExportable` (Kotlin, `android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/cipher/messenger/KeystoreInstrumentedTest.kt`)
  * `lostDeviceKeyFailsClosedAndNeverWipesTheVault` (Kotlin, `android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/cipher/messenger/EngineLifecycleInstrumentedTest.kt`)

## SEC-010 — Logs, analytics, crash reports, notifications and telemetry never contain plaintext, attachment contents, private keys, recovery secrets or auth secrets.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A3, A14
* **Scope tested:** Relay logs captured under full-trace and searched for fixtures/ids/ciphertext/keys; static guards on logging calls (Rust and Kotlin); Android logger accepts closed event codes only and R8 strips Log in release; notification text is built in Rust from privacy mode and vault state; push payload constant; an emulator session's logcat, relay log and pg_dump had 0 fixture hits.
* **Known gap:** OS-level logs/crash dumps outside our control; third-party SDKs are forbidden by a static guard but runtime behaviour of platform crash handlers is not tested; Android notification history retention is not tested.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_001_005_010_relay_wire_db_and_logs_contain_no_plaintext_or_private_keys` (Rust)
  * `sec_010_logging_calls_never_reference_bodies_or_secrets` (Rust)
  * `sec_010_no_stdout_stderr_or_dbg_in_production_code` (Rust)
  * `push_provider_receives_only_a_constant_content_free_wakeup` (Rust)
  * `only_safelog_may_call_android_log_and_it_takes_closed_codes_only` (Rust)
  * `r8_strips_android_logging_in_release` (Rust)
  * `notifications_never_reveal_content_while_locked_whatever_the_mode` (Rust)
  * `default_is_no_content_and_locked_vault_is_always_generic` (Rust)

## SEC-011 — The server cannot silently substitute identity/public keys without creating a detectable security event.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2
* **Scope tested:** TOFU pins + endorsements: key swap in directory, rogue/unendorsed device, forged endorsement, auth-key swap and KeyPackage substitution are all detected and fail closed; safety numbers/QR detect substitution.
* **Known gap:** A relay that lies from the very first contact is detected only if users compare safety numbers out-of-band; key transparency is not implemented.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_011_server_substituting_identity_key_is_detected_and_untrusted_until_acknowledged` (Rust)
  * `sec_011_key_package_with_substituted_identity_is_refused` (Rust)
  * `sec_011_malicious_relay_swapping_directory_key_is_detected_by_pins` (Rust)
  * `sec_011_malicious_relay_swapping_key_package_is_refused_by_client` (Rust)
  * `rogue_unendorsed_device_injected_by_server_is_untrusted` (Rust)
  * `safety_number_and_qr_detect_substitution` (Rust)

## SEC-012 — Sensitive operations use cryptographically secure randomness.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A11
* **Scope tested:** Static guard forbids non-CSPRNG sources and restricts OS RNG calls to approved modules; per-attachment keys/nonces are fresh.
* **Known gap:** Randomness quality itself cannot be tested; relies on the OS CSPRNG (getrandom) and the OpenMLS RustCrypto provider.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_012_no_non_cryptographic_or_ad_hoc_randomness` (Rust)
  * `sec_012_direct_os_rng_calls_only_in_approved_places` (Rust)
  * `each_attachment_gets_fresh_key_and_nonce` (Rust)

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A5, A12
* **Scope tested:** Bad signatures/replays/skew/audience/tampered bodies are rejected without state change; tampered envelopes, keystore blobs and records error out.
* **Known gap:** None at this scope.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_013_authentication_failures_fail_closed` (Rust)
  * `tampered_device_envelope_fails_closed` (Rust)
  * `sec_010_malicious_member_adding_unapproved_device_is_rejected_fail_closed` (Rust)

## SEC-014 — Replay of previously accepted protocol messages does not produce duplicate valid state transitions.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A12
* **Scope tested:** Client-side replay cache and MLS secret-tree both refuse replays (commits do not advance the epoch twice); relay refuses replayed signed requests and dedups message ids even after ack.
* **Known gap:** After the queue TTL expires the relay may accept the same message id again; the client replay cache and MLS then reject it. The client replay cache is bounded (8192 entries).
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_014_replay_does_not_produce_second_valid_transition` (Rust)
  * `sec_014_replay_rejected_by_protocol_layer_even_without_client_cache` (Rust)
  * `sec_014_replayed_signed_request_is_rejected_and_causes_no_second_transition` (Rust)
  * `sec_014_duplicate_message_ids_are_idempotent_even_after_ack` (Rust)

## SEC-015 — Any modification of protocol ciphertext, attachment ciphertext or local records is detected and rejected.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A4
* **Scope tested:** Bit flips across the whole message, truncation, extension, chunk reordering/truncation in attachments, record swapping.
* **Known gap:** None at this scope.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_015_modified_ciphertext_is_rejected_at_every_byte_position_sample` (Rust)
  * `modified_ciphertext_is_rejected_everywhere` (Rust)
  * `truncation_extension_and_reordering_detected_even_if_hash_is_recomputed` (Rust)
  * `malformed_and_truncated_ciphertext_rejected` (Rust)

## SEC-016 — No silent downgrade of key protection, KDF cost, or transport security.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A5, A6, A7
* **Scope tested:** Provisioning fails below the minimum protection level (software keystore only with explicit opt-in + event); stored KDF params below the floor are refused; https-only endpoints; relay refuses to start without TLS except explicit loopback dev mode.
* **Known gap:** Android NSC/TLS policy is checked by static guards and an installed-package check; a hostile CA / MITM against the app was NOT TESTED. Release build refusing the software Keystore is checked in the release gate (SECURITY_TESTING §7), on an emulator only.
* **Tests:**
  * `sec_016_provisioning_fails_closed_when_keystore_is_too_weak_and_never_silently_downgrades` (Rust)
  * `kdf_parameter_downgrade_in_storage_fails_closed` (Rust)
  * `plain_http_and_odd_urls_are_rejected` (Rust)
  * `tls_is_mandatory_unless_loopback_dev` (Rust)
  * `no_cleartext_http_or_tls_downgrade_in_production_code` (Rust)
  * `manifest_is_locked_down` (Rust)
  * `network_security_config_is_system_trust_only_in_release` (Rust)
  * `transport_is_tls13_only_with_no_redirects_and_no_custom_trust` (Rust)

## SEC-028 — Restoring an older copy of the app's local storage is detected and refused (monotonic generation held outside the data directory); the vault is not used afterwards.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A6, A7, A13, A16
* **Scope tested:** Core vault tests (device-key and PIN-only vaults, normal use never trips it, in-vault forgery impossible, reset overtakes a stale counter) and, on the emulator, the real Keystore counter plus a rollback through the real native library. On the emulator the real app was attacked by restoring an older vault.db after further use: refused with a rollback-specific message (EXERCISED, not automated).
* **Known gap:** The counter lives in the system keystore database, not in hardware: an attacker who runs code as the app or has root can edit it. A snapshot taken and restored inside ONE unlocked session (no lock/unlock in between) is not detected. Restoring a stale copy together with deleting the counter keys defeats it. Individual record rollback inside a newer vault is detected only through the generation, not per record. Not tested on a physical device.
* **Tests:**
  * `restoring_an_older_vault_file_is_detected_and_refused` (Rust)
  * `rollback_is_detected_for_pin_only_vaults_too` (Rust)
  * `normal_use_never_trips_the_rollback_check` (Rust)
  * `an_attacker_cannot_forge_a_higher_generation_inside_the_vault` (Rust)
  * `a_fresh_install_over_a_stale_counter_is_not_flagged` (Rust)
  * `theGenerationCounterIsMonotonicAndNeverLowers` (Kotlin, `android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/cipher/messenger/KeystoreInstrumentedTest.kt`)
  * `restoringAnOlderCopyOfTheVaultIsRefusedAsRolledBack` (Kotlin, `android/app/src/androidTest/java/app/cipher/messenger/EngineLifecycleInstrumentedTest.kt`)

  * `when_the_peers_relay_is_down_messages_stay_pending_and_are_delivered_after_it_returns` (Rust)
  * `groups_and_commits_with_a_peer_on_another_relay_are_refused_not_improvised` (Rust)

## MR-006 — Cross-relay attachments (image, PDF, video, voice, arbitrary file, thumbnails) are encrypted before upload, stored by both relays as ciphertext only, downloaded by the recipient from his own relay, and fail closed when tampered, truncated, swapped or missing; uploads need a live capability and respect per-capability and global quotas.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A3, A18
* **Scope tested:** Two relays + databases; files up to ~1 MB in tests; limits in code are 101 MiB per blob.
* **Known gap:** No resumable/chunked upload: an interrupted upload restarts from zero and leaves an unreferenced blob until its 14-day TTL. Whole blob buffered by the relay (bounded by 8 concurrent uploads). Large-video streaming and parser-bomb behaviour of platform decoders are not covered (ST-034).
* **Tests:**
  * `text_image_pdf_video_voice_and_arbitrary_files_cross_relays_and_each_relay_stores_only_ciphertext` (Rust)
  * `tampered_truncated_swapped_and_missing_blobs_at_the_recipients_relay_fail_closed` (Rust)
  * `uploads_to_a_foreign_relay_need_a_live_capability_and_respect_quota` (Rust)
  * `a_transfer_interrupted_by_the_network_creates_no_message_leaves_no_files_and_can_be_retried` (Rust)

## MR-007 — Metadata exposure of first contact is measured: against the mailbox relay, a card-based cross-relay first contact exposes zero signed requests, zero initiator-to-target links, zero stored mentions of the initiator's ids and zero sender hashes.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A3
* **Scope tested:** Request contents and stored data only.
* **Known gap:** Says nothing about traffic analysis: timing, sizes and source address remain visible to the relay and to colluding observers (NETWORK_ADVERSARY_MODEL.md).
* **Tests:**
  * `first_contact_exposure_before_and_after` (Rust)

## MR-008 — A conversation that arrives as a message request gets its delivery receipts once accepted, and outgoing timestamps are strictly increasing so same-millisecond messages keep their order.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2
* **Scope tested:** Single relay engine tests (Phase 1 regressions).
* **Known gap:** Timestamps are strictly increasing per sending device only; interleaving between different senders depends on their clocks.
* **Tests:**
  * `a_message_that_arrived_as_a_request_becomes_delivered_once_the_recipient_accepts` (Rust)
  * `messages_sent_within_one_clock_tick_keep_their_order` (Rust)

## MR-009 — The Android TLS trust component cannot become an accept-all manager: the platform trust manager decides for every host without a pin, a pin compares the full SPKI SHA-256 in constant time with validity dates, and no other file may touch trust-manager or socket-factory APIs.

* **Status:** partial
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A4
* **Scope tested:** Source-shape guard (static).
* **Known gap:** The Kotlin component is NOT exercised against a real onion relay, nor on a device; only its shape is checked. Live Tor tests used curl, not the app (NETWORK_ADVERSARY_MODEL.md §5).
* **Tests:**
  * `the_pinned_tls_component_cannot_become_an_accept_all_trust_manager` (Rust)
  * `banned_apis_do_not_appear_in_app_code` (Rust)

## MR-010 — Under seeded fault injection (network flaps, responses lost after the relay executed the request, device restarts, relay restarts, clock jumps, same-tick sends) every message reaches the recipient exactly once, in send order, and ends Delivered; messages queued offline leave in encryption order so no generation is lost to MLS out-of-order limits.

* **Status:** automated
* **Threats (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md):** A2, A4
* **Scope tested:** Real engines, relay router and PostgreSQL; 8 single-relay and 6 cross-relay seeds x 70 steps; in-process transport.
* **Known gap:** Not exercised: PostgreSQL restart inside the matrix (covered separately by scripts/test-deploy.py), real network stacks, group conversations, multi-device. Delivery is at-least-once on the wire with dedupe by message id; a relay that withholds after answering `queued` is undetectable (ST-032).
* **Tests:**
  * `single_relay_delivery_matrix` (Rust)
  * `cross_relay_delivery_matrix` (Rust)
  * `many_messages_queued_offline_all_arrive_after_reconnecting` (Rust)
